key_insight: Hierarchical multipoint anchoring strengthens buried interfaces in inverted perovskite solar cells, improving efficiency and resistance to temperature-driven adhesion failure.
engineering_relevance: Reinforcing the transparent-conductor/SAM interface addresses a critical thermo-mechanical failure mode relevant to durable perovskite photovoltaics.
method: Pretreat transparent conductive oxides with a homometallic halide to guide ordered self-assembled monolayer (SAM) assembly.
Increase surface hydroxyl density to promote multipoint metal–oxygen coordination.
Use cooperative chloride-induced hydrogen bonding to reinforce interfacial anchoring.
evidence_signal: Devices achieved 27.3% efficiency (26.9% certified) and retained 94% of initial efficiency after 400 temperature cycles between −40 and 85 °C under ISOS-T-3 testing.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish module-scale manufacturability or long-term outdoor durability beyond the reported thermal cycling.
paper_title: Hierarchical interfacial anchoring for durable perovskite solar cells
